findings.reason: §6 must keep an assertion that the candidate search finds a known-present worktree string (e.g. a seeded scratch tracked file or a known offender) before an empty offender list is trusted.
findings.text: taking scan candidates from `git grep -l -a -F WORKTREE_ROOT` and passing only those to `worktree_path_offenders` removes the positive control that the current test carries (`test_the_scan_reaches_every_top_level_directory`, `tests/test_*:51`), so a git-grep that returns nothing — wrong cwd in the hook, git unavailable, or pattern drift — produces an empty candidate list and reads as zero offenders, which is exactly the fail-open the guard exists to prevent

findings.reason: the pattern is pre-existing and repo-wide and lies outside §3's census (files that named a worktree), so consolidating onto `root_dir` is a separate node, not a change to this plan.
findings.text: the repository root is re-derived in 358 Python files (`grep -rln 'rev-parse\|show-toplevel\|Path(__file__).resolve().parents' --include=*.py`), of which 0 import `root_dir`; the §3 Python launch scripts join this pattern (e.g. `docs/figures/forward-solve-api/coil-edit-nonconvergence/diagnose_open_axis_arc.py:7`, `docs/figures/cut-cell-current-attribution/exact-support-floor/audit.py:11`) instead of extending the owner

findings.reason: the guard keys only on the stable `reckon-worktrees` token, so drift in the project-pattern would surface as an unmapped-path report rather than silence; a drift check is belt-and-braces rather than a correctness fix.
findings.text: the worktree layout is re-encoded (`WORKTREE_ROOT = "reckon-worktrees"`, `_WORKTREE_PROJECT = re.compile(r"nova-[0-9a-f]+")`, `_WORKTREE_PATH`) while `reckon/crew/routing.py:463-470` owns that root and layout; the plan states the justification (nova carries no reckon dependency) but adds no test binding the one re-encoded token that must not drift

findings.reason: the shell census scripts (79 sites) cannot import Python, so the per-script idiom is unavoidable there, and the landed §3 node is not worth reopening for the Python minority.
findings.text: for the Python launch scripts the plan re-derives the root lexically (git rev-parse / `parents[N]`) rather than extending `root_dir`; the plan searched reckon and cites `repository_relative`, but its account of prior art omits the in-repo root owner

findings.reason: §2 is landed and §6 adds no CLI or refusal surface of its own, so the plan's remaining node is unaffected; §6 in fact retires two benchmark defaults, which counts toward the budget.
findings.text: `filepath relativize` and its `--check` flag add CLI surface (cli_options 0 this week) and §2's own text names no retirement or merge; only the §3 followup body names a retirement (the superseded scan in `tests/test_render_receipt_paths.py`)

duplicate_owner-1.reason: nova.definitions.root_dir is fixed at import time to whichever tree nova was imported from. Through the shared editable install that is the canonical checkout even when a script runs in a worktree, which a design-review round of this plan established. So it is the wrong owner for a run-time root, and the launch scripts resolve their own. Consolidating the repo-wide root idiom is separate work, as the finding notes.

duplicate_owner-2.reason: Residual drift risk, marked not plan-changing. The guard keys on the stable reckon-worktrees token, so drift in the project pattern surfaces as an unmapped report rather than silence. The layout owner is named in section 1.

interface_budget-1.reason: Section 2 has landed and accounted for its surface before it collapsed: one subcommand on the existing filepath group, not a new command. Section 6 adds no CLI or refusal surface and retires two benchmark defaults, as the finding notes.

reuse_search-1.reason: Same root_dir question as duplicate_owner-1: the import-time root resolves to the canonical checkout from a worktree, so it cannot serve as the run-time root. Section 3 states this.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §6 moves candidate enumeration out to `git grep -l -a -F WORKTREE_ROOT` and drops the current positive control, so the scan's reach becomes hidden behind an enumeration that can legitimately return nothing.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the repository root is re-derived in 358 Python files and no file imports the owner `nova.definitions.root_dir`; the §3 Python launch scripts join that pattern rather than extending the owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — cli_options 0, public_definitions 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds a `relativize` subcommand and a `--check` flag without naming, in its own text, what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites reckon's layout owner and the census, and reuses the realpath/git-root idiom already present in 79 shell scripts, but never cites `nova.definitions.root_dir`, the existing repository-root owner it could extend for the Python launch scripts.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the hook `scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit` is a justified thin caller of `filepath relativize --check`; git exposes no other commit-time hook, so a shim is the honest change.
